headings.title: Introduction to Electronic Communication in Nursing
headings.content: Electronic communication in nursing encompasses the exchange of health information, administrative data, and educational resources using digital tools. This includes electronic health records, secure messaging apps, professional emails, and telehealth platforms. Modern clinical practice relies heavily on these technologies to bridge gaps between shifts, connect rural clinics to tertiary centers, and speed up medical interventions. Unlike traditional paper charting, digital channels allow multiple practitioners to view patient notes simultaneously, reducing delays in treatment. Yet, this speed introduces risks regarding data privacy and message misinterpretation that require strict adherence to professional guidelines.

headings.title: Individual and Group Messaging in Clinical Settings
headings.content:
Nurses frequently use one-on-one and group messaging for shift handovers, urgent consultations, and administrative updates. Individual messaging suits private patient queries or direct instructions between a senior nurse and a junior colleague. Group messaging coordinates multidisciplinary teams, such as an entire ward staff or a specialized trauma response unit.

- **Direct Messaging**: Quick exchange between two clinicians regarding a specific patient issue.
- **Broadcast Groups**: One-way announcements from management to all nurses on duty.
- **Multidisciplinary Chats**: Collaborative spaces for doctors, pharmacists, and nurses managing complex cases.

headings.title: Video Conferencing Platforms in Healthcare
headings.content:
Video conferencing transforms how healthcare teams conduct ward rounds, nursing education, and telehealth consultations. Platforms like Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams enable face-to-face visual interaction regardless of geographical distance. In Nigerian healthcare, these tools help rural primary health centers consult with specialists in urban teaching hospitals without requiring patient transport.

| Platform | Common Healthcare Use | Key Feature |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Zoom | Webinars and lectures | Breakout rooms for small group training |
| Google Meet | Quick team syncs | Browser-based access without heavy downloads |
| Microsoft Teams | Enterprise hospital communication | Deep integration with electronic medical records |

headings.title: Digital Learning Management Systems (LMS)
headings.content: Continuing professional development and nursing student education increasingly rely on Learning Management Systems like Moodle. These platforms host course materials, assignment submissions, quizzes, and discussion forums in a centralized repository. Nurse educators can track student progress, grade submissions, and upload clinical guidelines accessible anywhere via mobile phones or desktop computers. Students must regularly check the platform for announcements, upload practical case studies, and participate in asynchronous learning modules that complement bedside clinical hours.

headings.title: Best Practices and Security in Nursing Digital Communication
headings.content: Using digital tools in healthcare requires strict adherence to data protection laws and patient confidentiality. Nurses must never share patient photographs, names, or clinical details on open social media channels. Passwords must be strong, logouts mandatory after every session on shared ward computers, and official hospital-approved applications prioritized over personal messaging apps. A common misconception is that deleting a message removes it permanently from hospital servers; digital audit trails often remain accessible for legal and institutional reviews.
